newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Brazil pressured on imports by Mercosur partners.
newsitem.headline: Brazil pressured on imports by Mercosur partners.

text.p: Brazil came under pressure Wednesday from Mercosur customs union partners Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay to drop its restrictive new limits on imports.

"Brazil is still not proving receptive to argument," said Paraguay's ex-Economy Minister Carlos Facetti, who stepped down just a few days ago but was still representing the host country at a meeting of Mercosur economy ministers and central bankers.
"We hope this meeting will produce a solution because Brazil's measures are affecting the Mercosur treaty."
Brazil angered its partners earlier this month by slapping limits on import financing for less than 360 days, effectively forcing Brazilian importers to pay cash.
Brazil was acting under pressure from a widening trade gap, but had to water down the new rules for Mercosur while it seeks a permanent solution for its regional partners.
The interim arrangement, which only lasts until July, means imports from the Mercosur can be financed up to 89 days for a maximum value of $40,000 rather than $10,000.

Paraguay called the urgent meeting of Mercosur finance chiefs in its capital Asuncion to discuss the issue, which Argentine President Carlos Menem will bring up with Brazil's Fernando Henrique Cardoso in Rio de Janeiro this weekend.

Facetti said after preliminary talks in Asuncion: "I would not talk of signs of change in the Brazilian position...but there is understanding that these measures affect the other members of Mercosur."

Argentine Foreign Trade Secretary Jorge Campbell, who flew to Asuncion Wednesday with Economy Minister Roque Fernandez, said the talks would "develop the analysis of the Brazilian measures and their effects on both economies."

He denied that Argentina was awaiting some "political gesture" from Brazil on imports: "I insist that what we want is to preserve the Mercosur dimension because Mercosur is a capital of which all four countries must take care."

The Mercosur Inter-Parliamentary Committee urged economy chiefs meeting in Asuncion to come up with "a mechanism that ensures previous consultation before the adoption of economic measures by every state that could affect its partners."
